title: Postpartum Care in the NICU Multi-Site Breastfeeding
official: Postpartum Care in the NICU (PeliCaN) for Maternal Wellbeing and Breastfeeding
summary:
Parents of infants in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) face unique barriers to long-term breastfeeding and lactation. The physical and emotional demands of having a critically ill or premature newborn combined with the stress, sleep deprivation, and separation inherent to the NICU environment make it difficult for many mothers to sustain breastfeeding and lactation, even when they want to. At the same time, NICU mothers are at elevated risk for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and poor health-related quality of life, which can further undermine lactation success and overall maternal wellbeing.

PeliCaN Multi-Site Breastfeeding tests whether a trained postpartum doula, working directly in the NICU can improve breastfeeding and lactation outcomes and support maternal mental health through 6 months postpartum. Participants are enrolled during their infant's NICU hospitalization to receive either doula support or standard care, depending on the study site condition at the time of enrollment (control vs. intervention). Mothers in the intervention group will receive lactation education and support, and emotional and informational support from a NICU-informed doula for up to 6 months. Mothers in the usual care group receive standard NICU clinical care, including access to NICU lactation consultants, without study doula support.

All participants complete surveys at enrollment and at 6 months postpartum covering infant feeding practices, maternal mental health, and demographic characteristics. The study asks two primary questions: (1) Does NICU-informed postpartum doula support improve breastfeeding and lactation rates at 6 months? (2) Does doula support improve health-related quality of life and reduce post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms at 6 months? A subset of intervention participants, NICU staff, and lactation consultants will also participate in qualitative interviews and brief implementation surveys to assess how well the doula program works in practice across participating sites.
conditions: LACTATION IN MOTHERS WITH PREMATURE NEWBORNS
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Delivery \<34 weeks of gestation and intention to breastfeed or provide their own breastmilk to their infant
* Postpartum parents less than or equal to 2 weeks postpartum
* ≥ 18 years of age
* English or Spanish as the preferred language
* No restrictions to visiting their infant(s) in the NICU due to a significant social service issue (e.g. incarceration)
* Not planning adoption
* The clinical team anticipates that their infant, or at least one of their infants if multiples, will remain in the NICU for a minimum of two additional weeks (to avoid anticipated infant palliative care and planned transfers).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unable to read or sign informed consent
* If the medical team believes that the infant may die or be transferred to another hospital within 1 week

Subjects that do not meet all of the enrollment criteria may not be enrolled.
